body: Mongolian licence plates are mostly white with a hint of red on the left side from the Soyombo symbol.

Mongolia primarily uses the Cyrillic script, but Latin and traditional Mongolian scripts can also be seen. Mongolian Cyrillic features the unique letters Ө and Ү, and the common use of double vowels. Note that Ө and Ү are also found in Kyrgyz and Kazakh.
All Mongolian coverage was captured with a large pickup truck, which is often visible in Street View. Key features to look for are a tent on top, red side-view mirrors, a snorkel, and roof-racks.

Mongolia is characterized by its vast steppe biomes, featuring empty grasslands or deserts with a general lack of trees. The landscape often includes rugged, rocky, or rolling hills, as well as rivers and lakes.
Mongolia has unique bowling-pin shaped white bollards with two red stripes around the top.
Mongolian infrastructure shows significant Russian influence, with common sights including wooden poles with stone block supports and white lamp posts. A unique feature is the 'ЗОГС' stop sign.
Mongolian neighborhoods are often separated by dirt alleys and wooden fences.
White, round yurts, the traditional homes of nomadic families, are a common sight throughout Mongolia.
Large herds of animals such as horses, yaks, cows, sheep, goats, and camels are very common in Mongolia.
Mongolia's Street View coverage is very limited, concentrated along highways and in large towns, with the highest density around the capital, Ulaanbaatar.
A useful clue for location is that the Google car's driving direction in Mongolia is generally away from Ulaanbaatar.
Mongolia's topography varies from flat landscapes in the east and south, to rolling hills in the north, and large mountains in the west.
Newer Generation 4 coverage in Mongolia is currently limited to Ulaanbaatar and western Mongolia.
Forests, primarily of Siberian Larches, pines, and birches, are found in northern Mongolia, often surrounded by grassy fields.
Small dirt tracks through flat, vast grassy fields are a characteristic feature of far eastern Mongolia.
Off-road desert coverage can be found in southern Mongolia, mostly south or east of Mandalgovi.
Southern Mongolia has a few paved desert roads.
Southwestern Mongolia is characterized by arid steppe rangeland with coarse soil, patchy grass, and small shrubs.
Dry, rugged hills and mountains are a common sight in far western Mongolia.
Lakes and rivers are more frequently found in western Mongolia.
Snow coverage is primarily found in the area around Ulaanbaatar.
Distinctive fall coverage with orange-coloured trees and grass is found in specific areas, mainly between Lun and Hatgal and around Ulaanbaatar.
The forest near Bugant is notable for its narrow dirt trails with close-growing trees, resembling a Russian landscape, and features many birch trees.
Crop fields are rare in Mongolia but can occasionally be found in the Selenge and Töv provinces near Ulaanbaatar.

Ulaanbaatar, the capital, is Mongolia's largest city, featuring modern high-rise buildings and bustling streets. Its suburbs are recognizable by vast yurt districts in hilly areas, and you can find both Gen 4 and Gen 3 winter coverage.
The Choir Highway, the longest paved road with coverage, runs from Nalaikh to the Chinese border and is mostly a desert landscape. A railroad runs parallel to the highway.
The main highway through Mandalgovi is also a desert road but can be distinguished from the Choir Highway by its cloudy skies, darker pavement, and the deep blue tent on the Street View car.
The Mandalgovi Highway south of the capital is characterized by extremely snowy and foggy conditions from a blizzard during filming. The car has a deep blue tent, and the landscape is flat.
The Millenium Road west of Lun has late fall coverage with distinctive orange short grass and a silver tent on the car. The coverage transitions to sunset as it heads west.

The Darkhan-Erdenet highway is identifiable by low rolling hills, tall transmission towers, and occasional crop fields. Most of it has winter coverage with a tentless car, light snow, and yellow grass.
The highway between Chinggis and Baruun-Urt is one of the few paved highways in the east, notable for its cloudy weather and very dark, freshly paved road.
A railroad runs alongside almost the entire road to the northern town of Khuder, which is a key identifier for this area.
The Street View car's roof racks can help divide Mongolia: racks with rubber inlays are typically in the west, while empty racks are in the east.
The spare tire on the Street View car helps divide Mongolia into four zones: a netted tire, a single strap tire, a tire with no strap, or no spare tire at all.
In the eastern grasslands, the Street View car is equipped with a light blue tent and a forward-facing snorkel.
For the eastern car with the blue tent, the layout of the orange roof rack straps can further subdivide the region.
Around the city of Chinggis, the car's tent will have red tensioner straps at the front.
North of Ulaanbaatar, the car has a blue tent similar to the eastern car, but with a backwards-facing snorkel.
The Street View car with no tent is found in and around Ulaanbaatar, typically on a northwest diagonal path. The car is always driving away from the capital.
The Street View car with a bright silver tent is generally found in central and northwestern Mongolia.
